sources.title: Quran boards
sources.note: Read for the wooden writing board (lawh, pl. alwah) of West African Qur'anic schooling: mahogany and baobab boards, ink of natural pigments mixed with charcoal and water, and the washing-off of the mastered text so the water can be drunk or used in healing. Names Nigeria, Cameroon, Hausa and Fulani, and the British Museum, Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Musee du Quai Branly, Walters Art Museum, Minneapolis Institute of Art and Hood Museum as holding examples.

sources.title: Tintinnabulum (ancient Rome)
sources.note: Read for the Roman wind chime of bells, often shaped as a bronze ithyphallic figure or a fascinum, hung near thresholds at shops and houses, under peristyles and by the bedroom; examples from Pompeii and Herculaneum, a number of them in the Secret Museum collection at the Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli.

sources.title: Triskelion
sources.note: Read for the triple spiral: Malta 4400-3600 BCE, Newgrange c. 3200 BCE, European Neolithic through La Tene, hoplite shields and Greek pottery from the late 6th century BCE, the emblem of the rulers of Syracuse, and the arms and flags of the Isle of Man. The page does not say whether the recurrences are transmission or independent invention, and the record citing it says so.
